transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yes, it's nice to meet you too. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is just this... this absolute exhaustion. But it’s not, you know, it's not like a normal kind of tired. I’m a manager, so I’m very used to long days and putting out fires at the office and just generally being on the go. I've been doing this for years, ever since I got my degree, so I know what a hard day's work feels like and I'm used to being busy. 

But this is completely different. I’m just exhausted in a way that sleep doesn’t fix at all. I’ll go to bed, I'll think I'm doing the right thing by getting rest, and I wake up and I'm still just bone-tired. It’s like sleep doesn't even touch it. And it’s making everything so incredibly difficult. Just getting through a totally normal workday feels... well, it just feels so much heavier than it should, like I'm dragging myself through wet cement all day long just to answer emails or sit in meetings. 

And then by the time I finally get home, just the idea of having dinner at home, something so simple that shouldn't be a big deal in the slightest, it just feels like this insurmountable mountain. I just don't understand why everything takes so much effort right now, because I'm usually the one keeping my team running smoothly, and now just getting through the evening routine feels like it takes everything I have.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Well, yes, I suppose I have. It's... it's hard to explain, but most days lately, I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling. It's like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts, you know? And it's not just a passing thought, it's this weight that just settles right in my chest the moment I open my eyes. I’ll just lay there in bed, looking at the ceiling, and I can already feel that the whole day is just going to be... well, just a slog. 

It’s frustrating because, like I said, I’m usually the one who’s upbeat and keeping everyone else motivated at the office. I'm the one who comes in with coffee and a smile, ready to tackle whatever crisis the clients have cooked up for us. But lately, even before my feet hit the floor in the morning, I just feel this overwhelming sense of... I don't know, just sadness, or maybe just a complete lack of joy about everything. 

I try to shake it off, I really do. I'll go through my morning routine, take a shower, make my coffee, try to put on a brave face for the day, but that heavy feeling just kind of follows me around like a dark cloud. It’s like all the color has just been drained out of everything. And it's not like anything specific happened to make me feel this way, which almost makes it worse, because I can't point to a reason and say, 'Aha, that's why I'm feeling down.' It's just there, this constant, dull ache of feeling low, day in and day out. It’s just so unlike me, and it’s really starting to wear me down even more than the exhaustion, if that's even possible.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. And that’s... well, that’s another thing that’s really been bothering me, because I’m usually such a creative person outside of work. You know, my job is so analytical and fast-paced, so my outlet has always been art. I usually love painting. I have this whole setup in my spare room—easel, all these expensive oils I’ve collected over the years, proper lighting, the whole nine yards. Usually, on a Sunday afternoon, I could spend hours in there just getting lost in a canvas. It’s always been my way to decompress. 

But recently? I just... I haven't even gone in that room. I just leave my supplies sitting there completely untouched. The paints are probably drying out, honestly. And it’s not just the painting itself. I used to love wandering through museum exhibits, too. We have that great contemporary art museum downtown, and I’m a member there, so I usually go to all the new gallery openings or just spend a Saturday afternoon walking through the halls. I love looking at the brushstrokes, reading the little plaques, just soaking it all in. 

But lately, I get the emails about a new exhibit, or a special tour, and I just delete them. I can’t even make myself care enough to go. It’s like the thought of getting in the car, parking, walking around... it just seems pointless. Even when I try to force myself, I just think, what’s the point? I won’t enjoy it anyway. It’s so strange to look at things that used to bring me so much joy, things that really made me feel like *me*, and just feel absolutely nothing towards them. It’s like that part of my brain just shut off completely.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?

No, no, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, I know I've been talking a lot about how heavy everything feels and how I just can't seem to find the energy or the joy in anything right now, but it hasn't crossed over into that territory. I don't want to hurt myself, and I certainly don't think life isn't worth living. 

It's more just... I'm frustrated that I'm not living it the way I usually do, you know? Like, I want to be back to my normal self. I want to be the person who manages the team and goes to the art museum and actually enjoys a nice dinner at home instead of just staring at the wall. So, even though I feel terrible right now, and everything is just this exhausting, gray slog, I still want to be here. I just want to be here and feel better. I haven't had any dark thoughts about ending things or anything like that. I just really, really want to figure out how to get out of this rut so I can get back to my life, because the life I have is a good one, it's just... I'm just not really participating in it right now. But no, definitely no thoughts of harming myself.
Did this start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

Well, that's the thing, isn't it? I've been wracking my brain trying to figure that out. I mean, usually when people feel this way, there's a catalyst, right? Like a bad breakup, or losing a job, or someone passing away. But for me? Nothing. I mean, literally nothing out of the ordinary has happened. 

Work is... well, work is always stressful, I'm a manager, so I'm always putting out fires and dealing with different personalities. We did have that big quarterly review last month, which is always a headache, but I've been doing this for years, so it's not like it was a shock to my system or anything I haven't handled a dozen times before. And my personal life is fine, too. My husband and I are doing great, the house is fine, there haven't been any major financial surprises or anything like that. 

It's just so frustrating because if there was a reason, if I could just point to one specific event and say, 'Yes, that's it, that's why I feel like I'm walking through molasses every day,' then maybe I could process it, you know? Maybe I could talk to someone about that specific thing and work through it. But because there's no reason, it just feels like my brain decided to short-circuit entirely on its own. I keep going back over the last few months, looking for some hidden trauma or some tiny shift that I might have missed, but there really isn't anything. It just sort of... crept in. One day I was fine, handling my team, planning museum trips, and then gradually, it was just like the volume on my life got turned all the way down. So, no, no specific event at all. Which, honestly, almost makes me feel crazier, because why am I feeling this way if everything is technically fine?
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for days or weeks at a time?

Well, yes, actually. I mean, it's not the first time I've felt this way, though I always try to convince myself it's just a phase when it happens. If I really think back, there have been a few times over the years where I've just felt... stuck in this kind of gray space. But the one that really stands out, the one I can remember the most clearly, was a few years ago. 

I remember it so vividly because it just dragged on and on. It wasn't just a bad week or a tough couple of days where I needed extra sleep. It was... gosh, it must have been about five months. Five whole months of just feeling completely low. I remember waking up every single morning and just feeling this immense weight, like my limbs were made of lead. I was so tired all the time, no matter how much coffee I drank or how early I went to bed. I'd sit at my desk at work and just stare at my inbox, trying to muster up the energy to care about the quarterly reports or the team schedules, and I just couldn't. 

And it wasn't just the tiredness, it was this overwhelming sense of not being myself. I felt like an imposter in my own life. My husband would ask me what was wrong, and I'd just say I was tired, because how do you explain that you feel like you've been hollowed out? I wasn't painting then, either. I wasn't doing much of anything besides going to work, coming home, and lying on the couch. It was like I was just going through the motions, day after day, week after week, for almost half a year. So, yes, I've definitely had this happen before. That five-month stretch was probably the longest, but it's the same feeling I have right now—just this heavy, exhausting, low feeling where I don't even recognize myself.
Besides that five-month period a few years ago, have you had any other separate times in your life when you felt depressed like this?

No, I really don't think so. I mean, I've spent so much time just turning this over and over in my head, trying to make sense of it all. You know, you start to question your own memory when you feel like this. You wonder, 'Have I always been this way? Is this just who I am now?' But when I really sit down and force myself to look back, objectively, at my life—my twenties, my thirties, starting out in management, buying the house with my husband—I don't see any other major black holes like that. 

Sure, I've had bad days. Everyone has bad days, right? Or maybe a bad week where work was just incredibly demanding, or I caught the flu and felt miserable and sorry for myself. There was that time in my late thirties when we had a massive restructuring at the company, and I was so stressed I thought my hair was going to fall out. I definitely felt down and overwhelmed then, maybe cried a few times in my car before walking into the office. But that was situational, you know? It made sense. And it passed as soon as the dust settled at work. 

But as far as this... this heavy, suffocating, gray blanket that just descends for no reason and refuses to leave? No. It was just that one really awful five-month stretch a few years ago, and then... well, and then whatever this is right now. Between that time and this time, I was fine. I was me. I was managing my team, I was painting on the weekends, I was going to the museum. I was completely normal. So, no, there haven't been any other separate times like this. Just the one big one before, and then now. It's just so bizarre how it can just hijack your brain like this, isn't it? Like, where does it even come from if it's not a regular pattern?
